whyThisShow: This is the show the Dead themselves endorsed by releasing it as the video document "Downhill from Here," and the community broadly agrees the band earned that choice. One reviewer placed it among the year's best, writing that "July was the hottest month since '87 and the best until March '90" and that "the Alpine run was the late-Brent era's hottest 3-day run". The second set is where the most sustained energy lives: one listener heard the China>Rider opener as "surprisingly fresh and inspired for such an old horse" followed by ensemble playing in Playin' and UJB that was "so on target it's easy to forget it's live". The show also closes a chapter: Push Comes to Shove turns up here for the last time, and one head who saw roughly fourteen versions called this the best of the lot. And We Bid You Goodnight, absent since Winterland's closing night eleven years prior, capped the evening.
listenFor: The Music Never Stopped in the first set is a specific target: one reviewer called it "just freaking nailed" and noted it as one of the song's best outings after more routine 80s airings. On Standing on the Moon, one listener flagged the line "A lovely view of heaven, but I'd rather be with you" as a lump-in-the-throat moment, with a solo that "brings the house down". The Space is worth your time: described as "very mystical and introspective" with Brent's effects doing something unusual right before the transition out. The SBD recording (identifier gd89-07-17.sbd.unknown.17702.sbeok.shnf) draws consistent praise for balance and clarity — one reviewer noted "everyone is nicely balanced unlike other SBDs I have come across from this era". Note that "Good Times" and one other track have cut-outs on this upload.
context: July 17, 1989 was the first night of a three-show run at Alpine Valley Music Theatre in East Troy, WI — a run the community has treated as a peak moment of Brent Mydland's final active years. The show was captured in a complete-show video taping and officially released as "Downhill from Here," making it one of the more thoroughly documented late-era shows. The SBD circulates under archive identifier gd89-07-17.sbd.unknown.17702.sbeok.shnf; a Sokolow matrix version also exists and has drawn positive notice. One reviewer noted the video release doesn't include every song played that night, with Row Jimmy, Masterpiece, Push Comes to Shove, and Music Never Stopped left off the commercial release.
funFact: And We Bid You Goodnight closed the show — one attendee remembered "a momentary scream of joy from the audience when the first notes came out of Jerry's mouth" before the crowd fell quiet to listen, marking the song's first appearance since Winterland closed in 1978.
headline: Brent at full heat, Alpine Valley, July '89.
